_note: HARD -- 'strong economy followed by continuous attacks', and 'attacks after eco has
been established' (AI_Player_difficulty.md).
THE ONE PLACE THE DIFFICULTY TABLE STOPS NAMING A CLOCK AND NAMES A STATE, which is
the whole design in one line. Easy and Normal unlock aggression at 10 and 7 minutes
because a handicap is honest about being a handicap. Hard has none, so its attack
rule waits on the thing the sentence actually means:
12 villagers, a mill, a barracks and 8 swordsmen
That is a definition of 'established', written down where it can be argued with,
rather than a minute count somebody tuned once. It also makes Hard MAP-SENSITIVE in
the right direction: on a poor map it attacks later, because it genuinely is not
ready -- which is what the owner was asking for when they ruled out ticks.
THE ECONOMY IS THE DIFFICULTY. Hard trains to 16 villagers before it thinks about
an army at all, where Easy stops at 7. That single number is worth more than any
amount of extra military rules: a bot with twice the income can replace what it
loses, and 'continuous attacks' is a consequence of being able to afford them
rather than a separate behaviour. The standing orders already send every idle
soldier back out, so continuity is free once production keeps up.
THE ARMY IS 20 SWORDSMEN, 10 ARCHERS AND 6 KNIGHTS, which with 16 villagers is 52
of the 55 population 9 houses and a town centre allow. Cavalry is what Hard adds
that Normal does not have at all (project owner, 2026-08-27), and the stable rule
is gated on age 3 for the same reason the archery range is -- a third production
building is worth more than a bigger number at one of them.
AN advance_age RULE MUST SIT ABOVE THE TRAIN RULES THAT SHARE ITS RESOURCE, and
this file learned it the expensive way. Reservation only protects a goal from the
rules BELOW it, so with 'train villagers to 10' above the advance, villagers ate
the food at 50 apiece and the 500 for age 2 never accumulated: Hard finished two
20,000-tick ladder matches still in age 1 and LOST TO NORMAL. Easy and Normal had
the two the right way round from the start, which is why they were unaffected --
and is what made the cause findable by diffing the files.
It does not deadlock the other way, either: the advance rule does not MATCH below
8 villagers, so it reserves nothing while the town is still growing into it.
CASTLES ARE AGE 4 AND EXPENSIVE, and the rule sits last on purpose: reservation
means a goal higher in the list holds its cost back, so a castle can never starve
the army that keeps the bot alive while it saves for one.
